title: Playing for White House interns with Tony Bennett
summary: The Kennedy-era concert moved to the Washington Monument, and Bennett sang That Old Black Magic without rehearsal.

blocks.x: You were taking about Pierre Salinger.
Thursday afternoon these – pages were a lot of them – . . .

. . . interns were invited to the White House. They would not know why they were coming, except it was Kennedy’s afternoon to entertain them. Word got out that I was going to be the entertainment. The lawn at the White House was flooded, and they could not keep that date there, so they moved us to the Washington monument. I don’t remember whether Jack Kennedy came or not.
Bobby was supposed to have been there.
I think there was talk. If he came, he came and went without our knowing it.
Security and all that was changed now. They said, “Would you play a song for Tony Bennett to sing?” I said, “Sure. What’s he want to sing?” Tony, without rehearsals - was it Night and Day?

That Old Black Magic. It came off just great. It’s on one of my records with different artists. It sounds like we knew what each other was doing. There were thousands and thousands at that, out in the open air. Then the next year – who’d we go for?
